reason: The graded content is supported by excerpt HO-10-bank. Point 1 is supported: fund policies commonly use $0.01/share and 0.5% of NAV, and the SEC called these 'generally used in the industry' in the Rule 2a-5 adopting release 'without making them a rule.' Point 2 is supported: 'Remediation follows the fund's own policy: the party responsible reimburses the fund, and material errors go to the board.' The excerpt also says the administrator's liability for NAV errors 'is decided under the fund's NAV-error procedures.' Point 3 is correctly optional and is a fair inference from the Citi example. That policy sets shareholder de minimis amounts and is internally inconsistent at the 0.5% boundary, hence 'quote the policy when precision matters.' The central error directly negates 'without making them a rule.' The scope (US, issuer/operator, mechanism) matches the excerpt, and the overlap rationale against QL-32 is sound. Tier A is defensible because the note ties the claim to the named adopting release, although only the note itself is supplied. Two fixes are needed. (1) The demand_source location cites 'pp. 72–73' of ic-34128.pdf. No supplied excerpt verifies that page range or that this URL is the Rule 2a-5 release, so the location should be restated without the unverified detail. (2) Point 2 should state who is reimbursed, matching the source ('reimburses the fund'). It should also make clear that both remediation elements are part of the minimum rather than illustrative.

key_points.minimum: These thresholds describe common industry practice in fund NAV-error policies, which the SEC recognized as generally used when adopting the valuation rule (Rule 2a-5) without making them a rule.
The fund's own NAV-error policy governs correction: the responsible party reimburses the fund, and material errors are reported to the board.
Precise boundaries and shareholder de minimis amounts depend on the particular policy, so the policy text should be checked when precision matters.
